content: Skin rashes may develop within the first four weeks of starting treatment with efavirenz. However, it can be difficult to distinguish between a common rash and a rare rash that may indicate a severe allergic reaction. Severe allergic reactions to this medication are rare. This is not an exhaustive list of potential side effects. If you are in the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. If you are in Canada, do the same. Before taking efavirenz, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other issues. Efavirenz has the potential to cause a condition known as QT prolongation, which affects the heart's rhythm. The risk of QT prolongation may increase if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other medications that can also cause QT prolongation. Low levels of potassium or magnesium in the blood can further elevate this risk. This risk may also increase if you are using certain drugs, such as diuretics (water pills), or if you experience conditions like severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. Efavirenz may cause dizziness, drowsiness, or difficulty concentrating. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or engaging in activities that require alertness until you are sure you can do so safely. Refrain from consuming alcoholic beverages. In children taking efavirenz, rashes may be more common and potentially more serious. Report any rash immediately to your doctor. Your doctor may prescribe an antihistamine for your child to take before starting efavirenz. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. Treatment with efavirenz can reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to your baby, and it may be part of the treatment plan for this purpose. However, this medication does pass into breast milk. Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Other medications can affect the removal of efavirenz from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. Conversely, efavirenz can speed up the removal of many other medications from your body, which may affect how they work. Certain other drugs used to treat HIV infection, such as elvitegravir or other NNRTIs (e.g., etravirine, nevirapine, rilpivirine), may also interact with efavirenz. If you are taking atazanavir with this medication, you may need to also take another medication, such as ritonavir. Efavirenz may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods, such as pills, patches, or rings, potentially leading to pregnancy. Discuss with your doctor or pharmacist whether you should use reliable backup birth control methods while taking this medication. Check the labels on all your medications, including allergy or cough-and-cold products, as they may contain ingredients that cause drowsiness. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as urine cannabinoid tests, potentially causing false test results. In the event of an overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Laboratory and/or medical tests (e.g., liver tests, viral load, T-cell counts, cholesterol, and triglyceride levels) should be conducted before starting this medication and while taking it. Keep all medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
